events.text: You speak, and water answers. An endless sea spreads under a sky that has never held a bird, and here and there an island lifts its back out of the waves to look at you. {pw_world} is mostly horizon, and you find you like it that way.

effects.log: Somewhere on the first island, the first tide goes out and comes back. It will do that for as long as the world lasts.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: Somewhere on the first island, the first tide goes out and comes back. It will do that for as long as the world lasts. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You press your palm down and land rises to meet it: one great continent, plains folding into hills, hills into forests, forests into a coast that goes on and on. {pw_world} has room for a great many roads.

effects.log: The first river finds its way to the sea on its own. You did not have to tell it how.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: The first river finds its way to the sea on its own. You did not have to tell it how. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You let go of the ground before there is any. Islands of rock and grass drift in an open sky, roots trailing below them like the beards of old men, waterfalls pouring off their edges into clouds. {pw_world} has no bottom, and no one there will ever need one.

effects.log: Two of the islands drift close, touch, and decide to stay together. You did not plan that either.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: Two of the islands drift close, touch, and decide to stay together. You did not plan that either. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You think of height, and {pw_world} becomes mountains: ridge after ridge, peaks above peaks, valleys so deep the morning reaches them at noon. Every summit looks like a place someone will one day climb to ask you something.

effects.log: Snow falls on the highest peak for the first time. It is very quiet, being a god.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: Snow falls on the highest peak for the first time. It is very quiet, being a god. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: The first life of {pw_world} is not small. {pw_beast} wakes on the new ground, shakes the dust of making from its body, and looks up at the sky where you are. It is the first creature that ever knew it was made. Behind it, smaller beasts begin to stir.

choices.text: Give it a name of your own

effects.log: You name it, and the name settles on it like a mantle. Its children will carry that name for ten thousand years.
It roars once, and that is its name. You are oddly proud.

events.text: The first life of {pw_world} is green. Moss creeps over the bare stone, grass follows, and then trees, patient and enormous, until the whole world breathes. No one is there to see it yet. That is all right. The trees are not in a hurry.

effects.log: You plant a single seed with your own hand. Of all the trees in the world, it will be the oldest.
You watch a forest grow the way a mortal watches a fire. Time passes very pleasantly.

events.text: The first people of {pw_world} open their eyes: {pw_people}. They stand, unsteady, and look at one another, and then, all at once, up. They do not know your name. They know someone is there.

effects.log: You say one word to them. They argue about what it meant for the next thousand years, which is how you know they are people.

choices.text: Leave them to find their own words

effects.log: You say nothing. By evening they have invented a word for "sky" and a word for "who is up there".

events.text: You breathe on the fields of {pw_world}. Wheat stands up straighter, orchards bend under fruit, and in a hundred villages people who were counting their grain stop counting. Someone leaves the first sheaf on a stone, for whoever is listening.

effects.log: The harvest feast is the loudest thing in the world this year. You can hear it from where you are.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: The harvest feast is the loudest thing in the world this year. You can hear it from where you are. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You lay a quiet hand over the kingdoms of {pw_world}. Armies that were marching stop to rest, and find they do not want to start again. Envoys ride. A treaty is signed in a tent with too few chairs.

effects.log: For a while, nobody in the world is at war. Generals take up gardening. Some are very bad at it.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: For a while, nobody in the world is at war. Generals take up gardening. Some are very bad at it. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You let a little of what you know fall into {pw_world} like rain. A scholar wakes with a new number in her head; a potter finds a glaze nobody has made; a child asks a question so good that the elders write it on a wall.

effects.log: The world grows a little wiser this year. It will not remember why.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: The world grows a little wiser this year. It will not remember why. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You are angry with {pw_world}, and the sky is the first to know. A storm walks across the land for nine days. Roofs come down, rivers run wide, and the people hide in their temples and promise to be better.

effects.log: When the storm passes, the temples are fuller than they have been in a century. Fear is a kind of faith. You are not sure it is the kind you wanted.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: When the storm passes, the temples are fuller than they have been in a century. Fear is a kind of faith. You are not sure it is the kind you wanted. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You hold back the rain from {pw_world}. A season, then a year. The wells sink. Caravans turn back. A kingdom that had grown proud of its granaries learns how long a granary lasts.

effects.log: One kingdom does not survive the dry years. The others remember, and pray more carefully.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: One kingdom does not survive the dry years. The others remember, and pray more carefully. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You let the ground of {pw_world} shrug. Only once, only a little, and still the greatest palace in the world cracks down the middle, and the crown that sat in it rolls into the dust.

effects.log: The greatest kingdom falls, and smaller ones rise out of its pieces. They all build their new temples on solid rock.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: The greatest kingdom falls, and smaller ones rise out of its pieces. They all build their new temples on solid rock. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: You walk into {pw_world} on your own feet. You take a shape they can bear to look at, and walk down a road between two villages, and by the time you reach the second one the whole world knows.

choices.text: Heal the sick who come to you

effects.log: You heal everyone who comes. There are a great many, and you do not mind.

choices.text: Sit with the children and answer their questions

effects.log: The children ask you whether you have a mother, and what the stars are, and whether you like them. You answer all three honestly.

choices.text: Say one thing to the priests, and leave

effects.log: You tell the priests one thing. They will spend a thousand years being sure they understood it.

events.text: You give {pw_dao} to {pw_world}. It does not arrive like a gift; it arrives like a season. One morning it is simply there, in the way water falls and the way people quarrel and the way the stars hold still, and everyone in the world feels it and nobody can say what changed.

effects.log: The world is a little more finished than it was.

choices.text: Stay and watch a while longer

effects.log: The world is a little more finished than it was. You watch {pw_world} a while longer before you turn away, and the world seems to know it.

events.text: The sixteenth law settles into {pw_world}, and the world is complete. It does not need you any more, and it knows it, and it loves you anyway. Slowly it rises out of your hands and takes its place among your stars, burning steadily, paying its faith across the dark.

effects.log: You watch it until it is one light among the others. Then you begin to think about the next one.
You give the star the name of the world. Its people will see it in their own sky, and never know why it is so bright.

events.text: You have been silent too long. In {pw_world} a new god has risen in your place: a voice in a mountain, a face on a coin, priests in new robes who say the old maker was a story told to children. They have taken {pw_temples} of your temples, and they are not wrong that you were gone.

choices.text: Let the world go. It will be theirs for good

effects.log: You open your hand. If they are happier with a god who is there, let them have one. It hurts more than you expected.

choices.text: Go down and face it. Win, and the world is yours again; lose, and you can face it again later

effects.log: You turn your whole attention on your world for the first time in a long time. The false god feels it, and is afraid.

choices.text: Not yet. It will wait for your answer

effects.log: You watch. The false god grows a little bolder. You will have to answer it, one year or another.

events.text: You come down into {pw_world} and the false god meets you on the steps of your own oldest temple. Close up it is smaller than its statues: a spirit of the mountain that learned to wear worship like a coat. Its priests stand behind it. Yours, the few who are left, stand behind you. If you lose, the world stays theirs for now, and you can come down and face it again.

choices.text: Let it be. Let the world go, for good

effects.log: You look at the people behind the false god, and they look happy. You leave them to it.

choices.text: Show its priests what it really is

ok.log: You do not strike it. You simply let them see it as you see it, and the coat of worship falls off, and there is only a small frightened spirit on the steps. Its priests kneel to you. You let the spirit go home to its mountain.

fail.log: The priests do not want to see. The false god smiles. For now it holds the world, and you go back up into the sky with nothing.

ok.log: You ask them to choose, and one by one they walk across the steps to your side. The false god watches the last of them come, and bows, and is gone.

fail.log: They choose the god who never left them. You cannot even blame them. You go back up into the sky.

events.text: A quiet century. The rivers of {pw_world} carry silt to the sea and nobody writes anything down.
In {pw_world}, a hundred years of weddings, harvests and arguments about the weather.
The roads of {pw_world} grow a little longer. A song about you is sung wrong in a new way.
{pw_people} tell a new story this century, about a god who watches from the sky. They are right.
No one lives in {pw_world} yet. The first life grows, and waits.
A hundred years pass in {pw_world} with no one to count them.
{pw_people} walk out of the first life of {pw_world} and look up at the sky. The world has people now.
{pw_kingdom} is founded in {pw_world}. Its first ruler builds a temple before a palace.
A new crown in {pw_world}: {pw_kingdom}, raised by a farmer who would not stop winning.
{pw_kingdom} falls in {pw_world}. Its last ruler goes to the temple and asks you why. You do not answer.
In {pw_world}, {pw_kingdom} breaks into quarrelling provinces. Their maps disagree about everything.
{pw_world} itself grows stronger: the world is {pw_realm} now. Its people feel it as a good year that never quite ends.
The temples of {pw_world} are full. {pw_temples} of them ring their bells at dawn for you.
In {pw_world}, children are named after you this century. Many of the names are wrong. All of them are fond.
In {pw_world}, priests in new robes say there is a new god, one who is actually there. People are listening.
{pw_world} has forgotten you. The last temple is a barn now. The children have a new word for the sky, and it does not mean you.

Your family takes you to the temple of the Maker for the first time. There is a statue of the god who made {pw_world}, and it is meant to be you, and it is not a very good likeness. The incense makes you sneeze. A priest pats your head.

choices.text: Stare at the statue for a long time

effects.log: Something about the statue troubles you all the way home. You dream of a sea with no shore.

choices.text: Ask the priest who the god really was

effects.log: "The one who made everything," the priest says, "and then was quiet." You find that you already knew.
The priest is scandalised. Your family apologises. You keep giggling all the way home.

events.text: An old priest teaches the children of the village the history of the world. The Maker, he says, {pw_record}. He tells it as he was taught: {pw_deed}. Every word of it is true. You know, because you remember doing it.

effects.log: He gets the reasons wrong, every one. The deeds are right. You walk home feeling strange in your own skin.
The priest frowns, then looks at you for a long time. "Who told you that?" Nobody did.

choices.text: Ask why the god did it

effects.log: "Nobody knows the mind of the Maker," he says. You do. You are not sure you agree with yourself any more.

events.text: In a locked hall of the great temple lies a relic of the first days: a thing that holds a little of {pw_gift}, the first gift the Maker gave the world. The keeper lets pilgrims look at it through a screen. When you look, it looks back.

effects.log: The keeper does not see your hand move. The relic warms, the way a hearth warms when its owner comes home. (The relic remembers you)
It belongs to them now. You bow to it and go, and the relic glows a little brighter for the rest of the day.

events.text: A band of devotees passes through your town, singing the hymns of the Maker who blessed the world. They hand out bread in the god's name, as the god once gave them a harvest. One of them presses a loaf into your hands. "The god loves us," she says. "Never forget it."

effects.log: She smiles as if you had given her something. Perhaps you have.

choices.text: Ask what the god is like

effects.log: "Kind," she says at once. "Kind, and far away." That is not wrong.

events.text: In the square, men and women in grey sackcloth curse the Maker. They tell the punishments one by one: the storms, the dry years, the cracked palaces. "A cruel god," their leader shouts, "who made us to be afraid." They burn a straw figure of you.

choices.text: Stay and listen to all of it

effects.log: You listen until the end. It is not comfortable. Some of it is fair.
You say the god had reasons. They ask you what they were. You find you cannot explain them in a way that would comfort a child.
You walk away. The smoke follows you down the street.

events.text: Something happens in front of you that could only happen in {pw_world}. The old people shrug at it: that is just the law of the world, they say. The first law, set at the making: {pw_law}. You remember choosing it, at a table that was not a table, a very long time ago.

effects.log: It holds. Of course it holds. You made it to hold.

choices.text: Wonder if it was the right law

effects.log: You lie awake wondering. By morning you decide it was. Mostly.

events.text: Deep in the wild country lives a creature the hunters will not touch: a descendant of {pw_beast}, the first life of the world. When you walk into its clearing, it does not run. It lowers its great head and breathes on your hands, the way its ancestor once breathed on the hands that made it.

choices.text: Rest your forehead against its own

effects.log: It stays with you until dusk. When you leave, it follows at a distance for three days, then turns back.
It bows back. The hunters who see it from the treeline tell the story for the rest of their lives.

events.text: In the oldest forest of {pw_world} there is one tree older than all the rest, planted, the foresters say, by the god's own hand. Its bark is like stone. When you put your palm on it, you feel a heartbeat, very slow, that has been waiting for you.

choices.text: Sit under it for a day

effects.log: You sit there from dawn to dusk. When you leave, you are calmer than you have ever been.
You keep the leaf for the rest of your life. It never withers.

events.text: The eldest of {pw_people} keep the story of the first morning: how they opened their eyes and looked at one another, and then up. An old storyteller tells it at the fire. When she gets to the part where they look up, she looks straight at you, and stops.

effects.log: She finishes the story with her voice shaking a little. Afterwards she gives you a cup of tea and does not ask anything.
She goes on as if nothing happened. You do not sleep well.

events.text: The ruler of {pw_kingdom} has heard that a strange young person in your town speaks of the god as if they had met. A messenger comes with an invitation: the court wishes to know the will of the Maker on a matter of war.

choices.text: Go and tell them the truth

effects.log: You tell the ruler what you would want, if you were the god. You are. The war does not happen.

choices.text: Go and tell them what they want to hear

effects.log: You tell them the god favours their cause. They go to war. You wonder, later, whether you have just made a god of yourself again.
You send the messenger back with a polite no. A god who speaks every time a ruler asks is not much of a god.

events.text: You dream of making the world: the land coming up under your palm, the first gift, the first law, the first life waking. You wake with your hands still warm and do not know, for a long moment, which of the two of you is dreaming.

effects.log: You write it all down. It reads like scripture. You hide it under a floorboard.
You try. It does not let you.

events.text: Priests of the new god come through your village to collect the temple tithe. They say the old Maker is dead and their god is the true one. They are quite sure. You can feel the false god behind them, like a draught from a door left open.

effects.log: You refuse. They write your name in a book. It is a dangerous book to be in.
You pay and watch. You learn their hymns, their prayers, the name they call it. One day it may be useful.

events.text: At the edge of the village there is a ruin nobody visits. Moss over carved stone; a roof half fallen in; a statue with no face left. It was a temple once. Nobody remembers to whom. You do.

choices.text: Clear the moss from the altar

effects.log: You work all afternoon. When you are done, a child is watching from the doorway, and asks who lived here. "Someone who forgot to visit," you say.

choices.text: Sit in the ruin a while

effects.log: It is very quiet. You find you are not angry with them for forgetting. You were the one who left.

events.text: It is the Day of Making, the great festival of {pw_world}. Lanterns on every roof, dumplings shaped like islands, children in paper masks of the god. The masks all have the same silly nose as the statue. You buy one.

effects.log: Nobody knows. Everybody tells you it suits you.
You light a lantern and set it on the river. It feels like writing a letter to someone you used to be.

events.text: A sharp-tongued scholar in the city argues that the Maker never existed: that the world made itself, and the stories of blessings and storms are only weather and wishful thinking. The crowd boos. The scholar catches your eye, as if you were the only one listening properly.

effects.log: You argue for an hour. Neither of you wins. Afterwards you drink tea together, and the scholar says you argue like someone who was there.
"Perhaps it did make itself," you say. The scholar looks at you very strangely.

events.text: A small child tugs your sleeve at the market and asks you, with total seriousness, what the god is like. You think about it for longer than the child expects.

effects.log: The child nods as if that were the right answer. Maybe it is.
The child is delighted, and runs off to tell everyone.

events.text: You walk the great pilgrimage of {pw_world}, from the first shore to the first temple, as millions have before you. At every shrine on the road the monks tell another of the god's deeds. You know how each one ends.

effects.log: You walk it all. At the end, at the first temple, you feel the whole world looking up at the same sky as you.
You turn back. You have been to the end of this road before, from the other side.

events.text: Outside town there is a field the farmers call the Gift: the soil there has been black and rich since the year the god blessed the world, and no one has ever needed to rest it. You walk through the wheat and it leans toward you.

effects.log: You put your hands in the soil. It remembers you.
You work beside the farmers all week and are paid in grain and stories.

events.text: Across the hills runs a long grey scar where nothing grows: the mark of the god's anger, the old people say, from the year the god punished the world. Children dare each other to touch it.

effects.log: You walk it end to end. You remember why you did it. You do not feel better for remembering.
You plant a pine at the edge of the scar. In your lifetime it grows waist-high. It is a start.

events.text: In the capital stands the greatest statue of the god in {pw_world}, a hundred feet of carved stone. The face is noble, wise and calm. It looks nothing like you. You stand at its feet among the pilgrims and feel very small and quite amused.

choices.text: Climb up and look it in the eye

effects.log: You climb the scaffolding at night and sit on its shoulder. The city lights look like stars from here.

choices.text: Leave a flower at its feet

effects.log: It seems only polite.

events.text: The blind oracle of the high temple, who has spoken to no one in twenty years, turns her head as you pass in the crowd and says, clearly, "You came back." The crowd goes silent. Then the priests hurry her away.

effects.log: You find her in a little garden behind the temple. She takes your hands and weeps, and tells you the way to the empty throne.
You slip away. That night you dream of a staircase that goes up into the sky.

events.text: Above the first temple of {pw_world} there is a stair that no one climbs: the Maker's Stair, the priests call it, that leads to the empty throne. The oracle said you would know it when you saw it. You do. The first step is warm.

effects.log: You set your foot on the first step. The priests at the bottom do not stop you. Something in their faces says they have been waiting a very long time.
You turn away. The stair will wait. It has waited this long.

events.arc: The Road Back to the Throne

events.text: Halfway up the Maker's Stair the high priests block your way. They are old, and frightened, and very brave. "Anyone may say they are the god," the eldest says. "Tell us something only the god would know."

choices.text: Tell them the first law, and why you chose it

ok.log: You tell them. The eldest priest closes her eyes, and steps aside. The others follow.

fail.log: The words come out wrong in a mortal mouth. They do not believe you, not yet. You will try again.

choices.text: Tell them the deeds the scriptures got wrong

ok.log: You tell them what really happened. The youngest priest begins to cry. They step aside.

fail.log: They shake their heads. You go back down the stair, and wait for a better year.

events.arc: The Road Back to the Throne

events.text: At the top of the Maker's Stair is the throne: plain stone, too big for a mortal, cold. Around it lie the offerings of ten thousand years, and the dust of all the years you were not there. From here you can see the whole of {pw_world}, every road and river and kingdom you watched grow.

effects.log: You sit. It is too big. Then it is not. (The sky of the world remembers its maker)

choices.text: Leave the throne empty, and go back down

effects.log: You touch the stone and go back down. Let them have a world without a god on the throne. You will be one of them instead.

events.arc: The Road Back to the Throne

events.text: Your village is on a small island in the endless sea of {pw_world}. The fishermen say the sea has no end because the god loved the horizon. You sit on the rocks at sunset and agree with them completely.

effects.log: You learn to sail, and sail further than anyone from your island has ever gone. There is no end. You knew.
You learn every song the old fishermen know. One of them is about you.

events.text: Your home drifts in the open sky of {pw_world}, an island of grass and rock with clouds below. Children here learn to walk far from the edge. You were always the one who sat with your feet over it.

effects.log: You make the jump. Barely. Your heart is still pounding a week later.
You lie at the edge and watch the islands move like slow cattle. You remember setting them free.

events.text: You were born in a valley so deep the morning reaches it at noon. Above it, the highest peak of {pw_world}, where the old people say the god stood to make the mountains.

effects.log: It takes eleven days. At the top, the snow has never been walked on. You leave one footprint.
You stay. Someone has to look up at the mountains, or what are they for?

events.text: The great road of {pw_world} runs from one coast of the continent to the other, and you walk a little of it every year. Every inn on it has a shrine to the Maker by the door.

effects.log: It takes a year. You come back older and full of stories.

choices.text: Open an inn by the road

effects.log: You open a small inn with a shrine by the door. You keep the shrine very clean.

events.text: You are old now, in the world you made. You sit on the steps of the temple in the evenings and watch the young people go in and out with their small prayers. Some of them you can still answer. You answer them quietly, without telling anyone.

effects.log: A young farmer's sick goat recovers overnight. He will never know why. You sleep very well.
You watch the lights come on across the town. It is a good world. You did well enough.

events.text: On clear nights the people of {pw_world} point at a few bright stars that do not move like the others, and tell stories about them. You know what they are. They are the other worlds you made, finished and far away, still burning their faith across the dark.

effects.log: You name each one under your breath. Each one feels like a friend waving from a far shore.

choices.text: Tell a child the true story

effects.log: You tell a child that each star is a whole world. The child believes you completely, which is the right thing to do.
